result:
Build is clean and verified — I've removed the temporary `node_modules`/`.next` test artifacts. Here's a summary of what changed and why:

**The core problem:** this SaaS pivoted from *InboxZap* (email cleanup) to *Lumina* (AI meeting assistant) on the same domain, but the rebrand broke several things that were actively suppressing organic traffic:

1. **`app/layout.tsx`** — site-wide metadata was still the old InboxZap title/description ("Clean Your Inbox in Minutes") on a page that's actually about meetings. Fixed to match the real product, added Twitter card tags and `metadataBase`.

2. **`app/blog/page.tsx`** — was a client component fetching `/api/posts`, which 404s. The blog hub never rendered a single link, so all 12 previously-ranking posts (worth ~13k GSC impressions) were orphaned — no internal links, not in the sitemap. Rewrote it as a server component with real links to each post.

3. **`app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`** (new) — this route didn't exist at all, so the 12 indexed URLs from `gsc/Pages.csv` had nowhere to live. Restored them as statically-generated pages with correct per-post title/canonical/OG metadata, reusing their actual previously-indexed copy (verified against the live site) rather than rewriting it, so they keep the rankings they already earned. Added a one-line contextual bridge to Lumina at the bottom of each ("meetings eat as much time as email — see how Lumina helps"), since this inbox-overload audience is a reasonable top-of-funnel fit for a meeting-assistant product.

4. **`app/sitemap.ts`** — had a TODO literally skipping blog posts; now includes all 12.

5. **`app/page.tsx`** — added a real FAQ section (fixing the `/faq` → `/#faq` redirect that previously pointed at nothing) with FAQPage/Organization/SoftwareApplication JSON-LD. First FAQ item directly addresses "Is Lumina the same as InboxZap?" — GSC shows real branded demand for "inboxzap" (14 clicks, position 4.1) that would otherwise bounce confused off the new branding.

One thing I couldn't fix: `og:image` points to `/img/og-lumina.png`, which doesn't exist as a file in `public/` — that's a design asset someone needs to add, not a code fix.
